scope: Read-only review of the added persistent character cache. No browser operation, server restart, product code changes or user-data mutations performed by this reviewer.
reviewConclusions: Cache lookup keys include the freshly authenticated account handle and avatar filename. The server independently validates both identity fields and the current raw-JSON SHA-256 before omitting raw content.

Client verifies cached bytes and response owner/avatar/hash before reconstruction. Changed card content invalidates the cached raw string; current server runtime metadata remains in every response overlay.

IndexedDB is an explicitly selected dedicated localforage driver, with no localStorage fallback. Lookup failures/timeouts, corrupt records, profile lookup failures and malformed cache envelopes fall back to a complete response. Persistence failures are caught and cannot delay UI publication.
The existing bundled js-sha256 implementation works without Web Crypto on HTTP. Independent tests compare its UTF-8 digests with Node crypto, including Chinese and emoji.

The lib.js dependency exports are initialized before script.js and introduce no reverse dependency to the new cache module. The actual localforage constructor internally handles driver-selection rejection.
Only /api/characters/get uses the new opt-in cache protocol. Existing headers/CSRF are passed through unchanged; identity uses a GET without a body; /all and unrelated APIs retain existing behavior.

A per-avatar latest-request token and original character-list object identity are both checked before getOneCharacter publishes a result, preventing stale responses after concurrent requests or account/list refresh.

resolvedFinding.description: The first cache version awaited optional storage persistence before returning. A delayed Alice response for the same avatar could arrive after Bob was published and overwrite the current character object.
resolvedFinding.resolution: Added per-avatar request tokens and original list-object guards at actual getOneCharacter publication; cache persistence no longer blocks UI return.
resolvedFinding.regressions: Four added tests execute the actual installed publication function or cache loader, covering Alice/Bob same-name cards, list refresh without another get, concurrent requests sharing a list object and blocked storage writes.

independentTests.skipReason: Optional installed-card test was not enabled; actual deployment and browser checks are recorded by the parent/transport agent separately.

limitations: This review does not itself certify the restarted HTTP endpoint, browser IndexedDB persistence or physical TauriTavern.
Local SillyTavern updates may overwrite the transport/cache patches; restore sources from the matching backups or revalidate after updating.
